∀ {A : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} {U : Type u_3} [inst : Ring.{u_1} A] [inst_1 : AddCommGroup.{u_2} V]
  [inst_2 : Module.{u_1, u_2} A V] [inst_3 : AddCommGroup.{u_3} U] [inst_4 : Module.{u_1, u_3} A U] {ι : Type u_4}
  (p : ι → Submodule.{u_1, u_2} A V),
  (∀ (i : ι), IsSimpleModule.{u_1, u_2} A (Subtype.{u_2 + 1} fun x => Membership.mem.{u_2, u_2} (p i) x)) →
    Eq.{u_2 + 1} (iSup.{u_2, u_4 + 1} fun i => p i) Top.top.{u_2} →
      ∀ (f : LinearMap.{u_1, u_1, u_2, u_3} (RingHom.id.{u_1} A) V U),
        Function.Surjective.{u_2 + 1, u_3 + 1} (DFunLike.coe.{max (u_2 + 1) (u_3 + 1), u_2 + 1, u_3 + 1} f) →
          Exists.{u_4 + 1} fun J =>
            Function.Bijective.{u_2 + 1, u_3 + 1}
              (DFunLike.coe.{max (u_2 + 1) (u_3 + 1), u_2 + 1, u_3 + 1}
                (LinearMap.domRestrict.{u_1, u_1, u_2, u_3} f
                  (iSup.{u_2, u_4 + 1} fun i => iSup.{u_2, 0} fun h => p i)))

rule: Use primary exactly when the declaration itself states or defines the source claim. Use supporting for prerequisites, constructions, helper lemmas, instances, or consequences that help formalize the item but do not themselves state it.
source_text: If f : ⨁_{i∈I} V_i → U is surjective and every V_i is irreducible, then some subset J ⊆ I has the property that f restricts to an isomorphism ⨁_{i∈J} V_i ≅ U.
